page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-96-lssd is a high-memory compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The machine configuration provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes 504 MB of Level 3 cache along with instruction set support for AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is provisioned with 744.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, and integrates 6,432 GB of direct-attached NVMe local solid-state storage distributed across 16 drives. No dedicated graphics processing units are included in this profile.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory-intensive and throughput-sensitive workloads. The platform achieved 7,676.9 GB/sec in cached small-block memory reads, 356.43 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads, and 170.8 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Synthetic compute assessments show strong multi-core scalability, posting a PassMark CPU score of 110,319.41 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,133.0. Single-core execution falls into the middle tier, with stress-ng recording 2,299.88, while extended CPU encryption tests and static web serving throughput reached the top ten percent benchmark bracket at 151.31 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration emphasizes balanced, high-density resource allocation where vast memory capacity and low-latency NVMe drives offset moderate single-thread processor clocks. With 6.4 TB of pooled NVMe storage and dedicated core allocation, the server avoids network-attached storage bottlenecks. This profile is suited for memory-resident databases, distributed caching clusters, large-scale Clang compilation pipelines, real-time analytics, and high-concurrency database operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-96-lssd is an enterprise instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs on a 48-core Intel Xeon 6985P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, supported by 504 MB of L3 cache and AMX acceleration. It integrates 744 GB of RAM (7.75 GB per core) and 6,432 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across 16 bundled drives without GPU hardware. Benchmarks demonstrate exceptional performance in caching, memory bandwidth, and parallel processing, achieving 170.8 million Redis operations per second, 110,319.41 on PassMark CPU, and 151.31 GB/sec static web throughput. Single-threaded metrics remain moderate compared to high-frequency tiers. With massive system memory and low-latency storage density, this configuration is technically aligned with large-scale in-memory databases, distributed key-value caches, parallel build environments, and data-intensive transaction processing.
